Subject: Before you store it, check it
Preview: A few minutes of tent care now saves a ruined trip later.
Body: You put the miles in this season. Before the gear goes into storage, it's worth giving your shelter a proper once-over — especially if it pulled duty in mixed weather.

The Northbay Ridgeline 2P (NB-TNT-02) is a 3-season tent built from ripstop nylon and rated for two people. At 2.1 kg packed, it's light enough that it's easy to overlook until you actually need it next spring. That's exactly when you don't want to find a problem.

A few things worth doing before it goes in the closet:

• Pitch it once in the yard and let it dry completely. Storing damp ripstop nylon — even briefly — invites mildew that degrades the fabric and waterproof coating.
• Run your fingers along every seam. If the seam tape is lifting, a seam sealer applied now takes 20 minutes and extends the life of the shelter considerably.
• Check the zipper teeth for grit or corrosion. A zipper lubricant (wax-based, not petroleum) keeps them moving cleanly through next season.
• Inspect the poles for cracks or bent ferrules. The Ridgeline is a 3-season shelter — not rated for heavy snow load — so any pole weakness matters when conditions push its limits.
• Store loosely in a mesh or cotton bag rather than compression-stuffed. This keeps the ripstop nylon from taking a permanent set.

Note: The Ridgeline 2P is currently out of stock. We're sharing the maintenance guide now so your existing shelter is ready to go when conditions are right — and so you know what to look for when stock returns.

The full care guide is on the site. One read-through is worth it.
